chunk_findings.detail:
The upstream-report offer is computed only on the two "append" return paths at the bottom of `bug_found`; the early return for an extending answer bypasses it entirely:

```python
    if chk.extension:
        return DD.extend(log, cfg, chk, "bug.found")   # returns before any offer is computed
    ...
    with log.transaction():
        extra = {... title, severity, scope ...}
        log.append("bug.found", bid, {"item": item, "summary": summary, **extra, **chk.fields})
    prior = st.bugs.get(bid)
    stored = prior.scope if prior is not None else "project"
    offer = upstream_offer(...)
```

Concrete input: bug `B123` already exists and is `scope="ddflow"`. Call
`bug_found(repo, summary="<the same summary/item as B123>", scope="ddflow", answer=<an Answer that extends the OPEN B123>)`.
`DD.check_add` sets `chk.extension`, so the function returns `DD.extend(...)` before `extra`, `prior`, `offer` and `more` are ever built. The returned outcome carries no `offer` key, so the CLI/MCP caller gets no "prepare an upstream report" line even though the reported bug is ddflow-scoped — the exact case the feature says must end with the offer. The same recurrence reported *without* an `answer` (auto-id path) does produce the offer, so the behaviour is inconsistent depending only on whether the caller supplied an extending answer. The same early return also means the `title`/`severity`/`scope` values that were validated at the top of the function are silently dropped on this path (they are only consumed by the `log.append`/`chk` code below), so a user who reports an extending bug as `scope="ddflow"` neither upgrades the record nor is told to file upstream.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py `bug_found` (extension branch, ~line 517 vs. offer at ~line 528)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `marks` construction prints `scope` unconditionally whenever the row has the key: `marks = "".join(f"  {r[k]}" for k in ("severity", "scope") if r.get(k))`. But the sibling surface in this same change (`reporting.py`, `show`) deliberately suppresses the default scope: `marks = [f"{k} {b[k]}" for k in ("severity", "scope") if b.get(k) and b[k] != "project"]`. Since `bug found` defaults `scope` to `"project"` (see the MCP handler's `scope=a.get("scope", "") or "project"`), every bug created without an explicit scope carries `scope == "project"`. Given `bug found --summary "x"` followed by any dedupe/search listing containing that bug, this line renders `... open  project` (e.g. `1. B1  bug  0.90  open  project`), whereas `show B1` for the same record prints only the severity mark and hides the default scope. The two surfaces of the same feature therefore disagree, and the default value leaks into dedupe output as noise. The dedupe marks list should apply the same `!= "project"` filter used in `reporting.py`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/dedupe_flags.py:110

chunk_findings.detail: The new scope/severity/title handling and the upstream-report offer are only reached on the append path. The `chk.extension` branch returns early, before `extra`, the `scope` normalization effects, and `upstream_offer` are used, and the `DD.Record` handed to `DD.extend` was built as `Record(kind="bug", event_kind="bug.found", rid=bid, title=title, body=summary, item=item)` — it carries neither `severity` nor `scope`. So when a user files a recurrence that the check decides to fold into an OPEN bug (`answer` extending it) with `scope="ddflow"`, the ddflow scope and severity are silently dropped from the record and the function returns `DD.extend(log, cfg, chk, "bug.found")` with no `offer` key, even though the stated intent is "When scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer to prepare an upstream report." Concretely: file bug X (open, summary S, item T) as project, then re-report the same S/T with `answer=extend` and `scope="ddflow"`; the outcome has no `offer`, and `st.bugs[X].scope` remains `project`, so even a later plain re-report (which the code's own comment says should still offer) will use `stored == "project"` and produce no offer either. The `.scope`/severity values the caller passed are lost entirely on this path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:517 (bug_found, `if chk.extension: return DD.extend(...)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent states the one-line upstream-report offer is produced only "when scope is ddflow" (mode propose); for the default `scope="project"` the api call `bug_found(..., scope="project")` has no offer to return. The `bug_found` tool previously declared `"payload": ("id",)` — a set of keys taken from the api result — and now unconditionally declares `("id", "offer")`. Given a normal call `bug_found(summary=..., scope omitted)` (which the lambda coerces to `"project"`), the api result for that call contains no `offer` key, while the payload enumerates it. Any consumer that projects the result through `payload` (indexing `result[k]` / requiring every listed key) then fails or yields a missing field on the *default* path, i.e. every bug filed without `scope=ddflow` breaks through MCP. If instead the api always emits an `offer` key (possibly empty) this is harmless, but the intent's "When scope is ddflow … ends with a one-line offer" implies the field is conditional and the payload should be too.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:1604 (`"payload": ("id", "offer")`)

chunk_findings.detail: `reporting.py`'s `show` deliberately suppresses the default scope with `if b.get(k) and b[k] != "project"`, but the dedupe listing uses `if r.get(k)` with no such filter. Since `bug_found` defaults `scope` to `"project"` (and the MCP lambda likewise passes `scope=... or "project"`), a bug filed with default scope carries `scope == "project"`, so a numbered dedupe row renders `... <state>  project` while `show B<n>` hides the same scope as noise. Input: `bug found --summary "x"` (no `--scope`), then a dedupe listing — the row gains a spurious `project` mark that the sibling surface omits, i.e. the two surfaces disagree on the default scope.
